data.name: BuildAlreadyRunning
data.value: A build is already running for this repository; a second one would be refused until it finishes.
data.comment: Replaces BuildItBackground and its command line while a build is in flight: the instruction to start one is wrong then, and a second sync exits 75 sync_busy against the gate. Said on the paths that tell a reader to build, not on the ones that return content. Printed on every call for as long as the build runs, unlike SyncNotSearchableYet: it stands in for an instruction line, and an instruction said once is missing every time after.

data.name: BuildItBackground
data.value: Build it (runs for minutes on a large repository, so run it in the background):

data.name: Days
data.comment: The top of the age ladder RecordedAgo carries: Seconds under a minute, EtaMinutes under an hour, Hours under a day, Days above it, one decimal throughout. A record left behind by a build whose process died is dated in days, and 2880 min is a number nobody reads.

data.name: Hours
data.comment: Part of the age ladder RecordedAgo carries; see Days. Follows EtaMinutes in taking a space before the unit.

data.name: LocationNumbering

data.name: LspNoLiveDocument

data.name: NavigationHeuristicCoversNothing

Semantic indexing ran and produced nothing; the sync output says why. Re-sync after fixing that: {0}

data.name: NavigationHeuristicMissing
data.value: HEURISTIC - this generation has no semantic.sidx, so go_to_definition and find_references fall back to bounded text matching while find_implementations and find_relationships refuse. Re-sync to build it: {0}

data.name: NavigationOverlayNotBuilt
data.value: NOT READY - this worktree has uncommitted changes, or a commit the published generation was not built from, and its semantic overlay has not been built, so go_to_definition and find_references fall back to bounded text matching while find_implementations and find_relationships refuse. Build one: {0}
data.comment: The third value of a field a reader scans. HEURISTIC would say answers arrive and are merely worse, which is false for find_implementations and find_relationships - they refuse - and precise is the promise #421 is about. NOT READY is spelled the way the semantic_navigation_not_ready token is, because that is what the next navigation call prints for this same state. The consequence clause is NavigationHeuristicMissing's to the word: the two states differ in what is absent, not in what happens. The trigger is described in commits rather than trees on purpose: two commits sharing a tree need no overlay, and then this line does not print.

data.name: NavigationPrecise
data.comment: precise is one of three values of a field a reader scans: precise, HEURISTIC and NOT READY. All three tokens stay English in every language; only the parenthetical moves.

data.comment: invalid_position: is a status token left of the first colon and stays English, like semantic_navigation_not_ready: beside it.

data.name: ProcessMemory
data.value: The process was ~{0} MB larger; it now holds ~{1} MB ({2}).

data.name: ProgressAnalysingProjects
data.comment: The one figure in the semantic phase that is a measurement rather than a guess: the project count is known before the first iteration, and every project is awaited in turn. The words are RoslynAnalysing's own in both languages, verbatim but for the full stop, so a reader watching the console and a reader watching index_status are never told two things about one loop - and `разобрано` is the verb that comment pins for this action. Written on the same elapsed-time throttle the console line uses, not per project: a two-hundred-project solution would otherwise rewrite progress.json two hundred times to say what a five-second cadence already says. No remaining clause, unlike ProgressChunks: there is no Rate row for this phase to convert it into time with, and 26 minus 12 is arithmetic the reader does not need done for him. Both holes are counts and stay invariant.

data.name: ProgressCopyingGeneration
data.comment: Copying a half-gigabyte corpus and hashing it twice, which GenerationStore.PublishIndex does with no callback of any kind: two copies, two checksums, a manifest and a directory move. Nothing here is countable and nothing here is fast, so the clause names the work instead of counting it. It replaces `not counted in this phase`, which said only that this surface had nothing to offer - true of the old build and useless in the state a reader reaches for it. Two clauses joined by `и` in Russian rather than by a comma: the one-line `Sync:` form already separates its fields with commas, and a third meaning for that character makes the line unreadable.

data.name: ProgressNotRecordedYet
data.comment: Says the gate is held and no progress record has been written yet - the window between a sync starting and its first write. On the one-line form above an answer it fills the figures slot, and 'started' is the antecedent of 'it' in the sentence below; without it SyncNotSearchableYet names nothing. On index_status it is the whole block, in the `Sync phase:` row rather than the figures slot: a reader scanning that row for whether anything is running must not find it missing. No age: nothing was recorded, so there is nothing to date.

data.name: ProgressOpeningProjects
data.comment: RoslynRestored's own words, and the second of the two steps in a semantic build that no counter can reach: OpenSolutionAsync is one call, about ten seconds on the run that produced #387 and longer on a large solution. What tells the reader the build is alive here is the age beside the clause, not the clause, which never changes.

data.name: ProgressPausedBackendUnavailable
data.comment: Stands where the ETA does on the one-line `Sync:` form, and only while the build still holds the gate: on a record left behind by a build that died, ProgressStoppedAt already owns the state, and a leftover pause would report a dead process as waiting for something. It replaces the estimate rather than joining it - a paused build writes rate 0 and no estimate by construction, so the slot would otherwise always read EtaCalculating, which claims an estimate is being worked out while nothing is moving. That claim is the defect: frozen counters under `calculating` made a backend outage and a dying build read exactly alike. The figures beside it stay at the count the pause began on while RecordedAgo stays small, because the wait rewrites the record on every rung of the ladder, and this clause is what explains that pairing. Words rather than the token index_status prints: there the row name `Paused:` supplies the word and the value column holds identifiers, here the only field name is the literal 'Sync: ' prefix, so `paused` has to open the value - it is what a reader who sees both faces maps them by. It names no component, and deliberately: EmbeddingUnavailableException arrives by four routes - the broker failing to start, the broker not answering, a job that failed with BackendUnavailableException while Ollama was serving throughout, and an Ollama that was never running - and the one fact true of all four is that the embeddings have not come back, which is also how BuildBackendAnswered states their return. One key per IndexBuildPause member rather than a generic clause plus a token, which is the enum's own rule; a second member gets a second key. Subjectless in both languages, like ProgressNotRecordedYet in the same slot - the Russian keeps its feminine agreement with сборка.

data.name: ProgressReadingRepository
data.comment: Planning: listing what is in the tree and hashing every candidate file, before a chunk exists to count. Short on this repository and not on a large one, and until now it was the first thing a reader saw said about a build - as `not counted in this phase`, which reads as an apology rather than as work.

data.name: ProgressRestoringDependencies
data.comment: The longest silence in a sync, and the one no counter can reach: `dotnet restore` is a child process with no per-item callback, and RoslynSolutionLoader.RestoreTimeout allows it ten minutes. RoslynLoading's own words, minus the entry point and the budget it carries - this slot has a phase name beside it and no room for either. What tells the reader the build is alive here is not this clause, which never changes, but the age beside it: WhileTheStepRunsAsync reports on IndexBuilder.TargetBatchDuration and every such line rewrites the record. Subjectless in both languages, like ProgressPausedBackendUnavailable in the same slot.

data.name: ProgressScipPython
data.comment: The sibling of ProgressScipTypeScript, and a key of its own for the reason stated there.

data.name: ProgressScipTypeScript
data.comment: One key per adapter rather than one clause with the adapter's name in a hole, which is IndexBuildStep's own rule and IndexBuildPause's before it: the surface is where a token becomes words. `SCIP typescript` is spelled exactly as AdapterLine spells it on the console, and stays English in every language - it is the adapter's identity, and AdapterLine is a deliberate English literal for that reason. Only the clause around it moves. The step is recorded before the process starts, not after it returns: an adapter is allowed 300 seconds by SemanticIndexingPolicy.Default, and what this key exists to end is a record that says nothing for five minutes of healthy work. It does not yet keep the record fresh through that run - #491 is that half.

data.name: ProgressStepNotRecorded
data.comment: A progress record written by a build older than IndexBuildStep, read by a renderer that has it. Says what is missing rather than what is happening, because nothing here knows what is happening: the phase is present and the step is not. Not `not counted in this phase`, which was this slot's old answer and would now be false - the step is counted, by a build that did not know to write it. It disappears from a machine one build after it is upgraded, and it exists so that the disappearance is visible rather than silent. Subjectless in both languages, like ProgressNotRecordedYet, whose name it echoes for the same shape of state.

data.name: ProgressStoppedAt
data.comment: Says a progress record was left behind by a sync that died: it exists, it is neither Completed nor Failed, and the gate is free. 0 carries the phase name, then the figures or the step it stopped on, then RecordedAgo, in that order on the one-line form above an answer, and the phase name alone in the `Sync phase:` row of index_status, where the figures and the step have rows of their own. The ETA is dropped on both, because it was the dead process's prediction of a remaining time nobody is spending; the step is not dropped, because it belongs to the phase named beside it. Subjectless in both languages, like ProgressPausedBackendUnavailable beside it.

data.name: ProgressSwitchingOver
data.comment: The pointer moving to the new generation, which is the moment answers stop coming from the old index and the only fact in this phase a reader acts on. Pruning superseded generations runs after it inside the same phase and is deliberately not named: it deletes directories the reader has no stake in, and a second clause would double the length of the line for the shortest phase in the build. If pruning ever grows a counter or a complaint, it gets a step of its own rather than a clause welded onto this one.

data.name: RecordedAgo
data.comment: {0} is an age carried by Seconds under a minute, EtaMinutes under an hour, Hours under a day and Days above it. It is how long ago the figures were written, never a claim that anything is still running: a killed sync reads as recorded 3.2 h ago rather than as a build. It tails the one-line form above an answer and, after the timestamp, the `Updated:` row of index_status, so one age is spelled one way on both faces.

data.comment: The LEXICAL ONLY token and the command stay as they are in both languages.

data.name: SearchIndexHeader

data.value: (STALE: built at {0}, the mainline branch is {1})

data.name: SearchIndexModel

data.name: StatusNotRefreshed
data.value: NOT REFRESHED - {0} files to re-read, over the inline limit of {1}

data.name: StatusStale
data.value: STALE - built at {0}, the mainline branch is now {1}
data.comment: The token and the ASCII separator are a contract; only the clause after it moves.

data.name: SyncDidNotFinish
data.value: the build stopped without finishing and nothing is running now. Until a sync is run again, answers keep coming from the same index as before.
data.comment: The end notice for a build that died rather than failed: a killed process never writes Failed, so it never reaches SyncStopped. Printed once, on the answers that return content, and only to a caller that was already told this build was running - that caller is holding SyncNotSearchableYet's promise of a finish that is not coming. A caller who never heard it start sees today's answer unchanged: a record nobody clears would otherwise ride above every search answer for weeks. Lower case: it follows the literal 'Sync: ' prefix.

data.name: SyncEnded
data.value: the build finished. Answers from here on use the index it published.
data.comment: Printed once, on the first answer after the phase reaches Completed. Having told a caller that answers come from the last published index, the product owes it the moment that stops being true. Lower case: it follows the literal 'Sync: ' prefix.

data.name: SyncNotSearchableYet
data.value: Until it finishes, answers come from the last index it published.
data.comment: Said once per build, on the answers that return content. The figures alone do not say what they mean for this answer.

data.name: SyncStopped
data.value: the build ended in failure. Run a sync again - its output says why.
data.comment: The counterpart of SyncEnded for a build that failed - only when the record itself says Failed. A killed build never writes that; SyncDidNotFinish is its counterpart. Lower case: it follows the literal 'Sync: ' prefix.

data.name: TooBigForToolCall
data.value: A refresh this size runs for minutes, so it does not belong inside a tool call.

data.name: ToolFailed
data.comment: 0 is the tool name and is never translated. One key for all eight tools.

data.name: UpdateAvailable
data.comment: The `Update:` label and its padding stay literal, aligned to the same column as the rest.

data.name: WhileItRuns
data.value: While it runs, every search and navigation answer says how far it has got; index_status adds the rate in chunks/s while it embeds.
data.comment: The first clause is unchanged and stays true: an answer that rides above content still says how far the build has got, and since IndexBuildStep it says so in every phase rather than in two. The second clause gained its condition. index_status prints Rate and ETA only where CountsChunks admits the phase, which is embedding and nothing else, and a sentence promising a rate to a reader watching a ten-minute Roslyn restore would be promising a row that is not there.
